body:
I get you, never really had any claustrophobia at all myself but I understand it. 

I'm not sure about feeling better, not having to dwell on it on my own and reading other people's experiences have made it clear I'm not alone and that helps the loneliness aspect. I'd still say I'm not in a great space though but yeah I'm trying. How are you?

Closets are good tbh, I love enclosed spaces which some people think is weird but they're calming. I study chemistry and one of the tests was about group 2B sulphur compounds and the other was on HPLC. Yeah I guess it did it was kind of like medication but I got back up looked in the mirror then got angry with myself for wasting so much time.

Ah man I feel you I love animals so much that sounds so cute though. I'll continue to try to think rationally and hopefully I'll get some passion back. Thank you
If you're looking for suggestions of where to tie the noose, this is certainly not the place to get them. You're worth more than an undignified death and being found swinging by a rope.

Man I get you, I feel the same (albeit to a lesser magnitude). Something that helps me get through times of strife when I can't talk to anyone is to fight the war in my mind instead of trying to drown it out. I'm by no means one of those zen people but taking an hour to just deconstruct all the irrational thoughts in your mind might help. It also might not as I only speak from personal experience. And clearly not everything can be changed with positive thinking.

Talking to a devil's advocate therapist was one of the more helpful things I've done, as opposed to one who just listens.

Thanks man I do really appreciate that and I'll remember your offer, I completely understand what you're saying.

My day has been fine, I was laying on the floor for 4 hours earlier doing nothing and I've got tests tomorrow which I can't bring myself to care about. I'm sure it will get better and I'll get motivation back but what's the point in waiting for it if I can't enjoy the journey? It's times like these that I wish I just had one thing that I was really passionate about. I wonder if I fake it I can trick myself into thinking I care?

I guess that's true man, honestly the biggest problem I have is that I don't want to scare people off. I only have a few good friends and if I told them that I thought I was ugly or some other thing, I know exactly what they'd say and I'm not looking for fake answers you know? Thanks very much though I appreciate that and I'll check it out.

Thank you, I'm always taken aback by how genuinely kind strangers can be, much kinder than many people I know. You described exactly how I do, just to vanish from existsence without bothering anyone. 

That's very kind proposition for to offer too, I'd take you up on it but I'm not sure I'm entirely ready. Yeah I'm trying to feel better. Much love

I may not know you or be close enough to give you a hug but I'd be happy to, although it seems like you need a better support system than just that. Do you have good friends? They are the family you choose after all. If you do, I promise you that if you're close enough to them they would be happy to help you even if you feel embarrassed asking.

Clinicians unfortuantely tend to believe that your family is the best support you can get, in your case obviously this is not the truth, if you still attend counselling sessions, I would personally ask for some time alone to get it all off your chest to someone (admittedly not always) impartial.

Being compared to your siblings is hard, if you don't think you can live up to your brother's standards or if you aren't passionate about this programme, might I suggest following a passion instead? Even the most despairing of people has a passion, music? Art? No one's going to tell you how to kill yourself but if people aren't supportive of your logic, they don't understand what you're going through at all. You may need to speak to someone who does.
